message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling (both under her own name and her pseudonym Robert Galbraith):

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; introduces the Chamber of Secrets and the Basilisk. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Features Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | The Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s interference. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Introduces the Half‑Blood Prince’s potions book and key backstory. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | The epic conclusion to the series. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable released as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut of the private‑detective series featuring Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Midnight Library** | 2020 | A speculative fiction novel about a library that lets you explore alternate lives. |

These titles span Rowling’s most celebrated works—from the beloved Harry Potter saga to her ventures into adult fiction and mystery writing.
